definitions.explanation: A blood vessel that carries deoxygenated blood back to the heart.

examples.japanese: {静脈|じょうみゃく}から{採血|さいけつ}する。
examples.english: They draw blood from a vein.

examples.japanese: {静脈|じょうみゃく}{注射|ちゅうしゃ}を{受|う}けた。
{腕|うで}の{静脈|じょうみゃく}が{浮|う}き{出|で}ている。
examples.english: The veins in my arm are visible.

notes:
{静脈|じょうみゃく} is the medical term for veins—blood vessels that carry deoxygenated blood back to the heart.

MEDICAL COMPOUNDS:
- {静脈|じょうみゃく}{注射|ちゅうしゃ}: intravenous injection (IV)
- {静脈|じょうみゃく}{瘤|りゅう}: varicose veins
- {静脈|じょうみゃく}{血|けっ}{栓|せん}: venous thrombosis

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {静脈|じょうみゃく}から{採血|さいけつ}する: to draw blood from a vein
- {静脈|じょうみゃく}が{浮|う}き{出|で}る: veins are visible/prominent

CONTRAST:
- {静脈|じょうみゃく}: vein (carries blood TO the heart)
- {動脈|どうみゃく}: artery (carries blood FROM the heart)

KANJI:
{静|せい} (quiet/still) + {脈|みゃく} (pulse/vein) - veins have less pressure than arteries.
